transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Good morning, thank you for calling S-Net Customer Services, you are speaking with Callum. How can I help?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hello Callum, my name is Zbigniew. I cancelled my S-Net broadband contract back in July when I moved flat, but you have still taken £44 a month for August, September, and October!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before I look at any billing history, I need to verify your identity. Confirm your previous installation address and the four-digit PIN on the account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The previous installation address was 14B Station Approach, Reading, RG1 1NB, and my four-digit PIN is 3049.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And confirm the answer to your security question, which is your mother's maiden name.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Kowalska. Look, that is £132 in total that S-Net has taken out of my current account after my contract ended and after I posted the router back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have the account on my screen now. Let me ask you a few specific questions to check what happened with the termination order.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, ask whatever you need, I have all the paperwork and bank statements right in front of me.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What exact date did your broadband cease order complete, and how did you submit the cancellation notice to us?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I phoned your cancellations team on the 2nd of June to give thirty days notice, and the cease order completed on the 4th of July.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Did you receive an automated cease confirmation reference number by email when the line was disconnected on the 4th of July?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I have the email printed right here. The disconnection reference number is `CEA-902184-SN`, dated 4th of July at 11:14 AM.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And when you returned the S-Net Hub router, what date did you post it and do you have the Royal Mail Tracked 48 barcode number?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I posted it on the 8th of July from Reading Central Post Office using your pre-paid returns label. The Royal Mail tracking number is `JB-4491-0028-5GB`.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What date does the Royal Mail tracking page show that parcel was delivered to our National Returns Warehouse in Swindon?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shows delivered and signed for at the S-Net Swindon dock on the 10th of July at 09:42 AM, yet you kept billing me £44 every single month!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What were the exact calendar dates that the three Direct Debit payments left your bank account, and what payment reference appeared on your bank statement?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: They came out on the 15th of August, the 15th of September, and the 15th of October under the reference `SNET-BB-8839201`.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Wait a minute.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am looking at the cease workflow table on the system now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You just disappeared for nearly a minute without saying what you were doing! Did you find the cease order?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The line cease `CEA-902184-SN` completed on the Openreach wholesale side on the 4th of July, so the physical fibre port at 14B Station Approach was stopped.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Then why on earth has the billing system carried on taking money from my bank for three months after the line was stopped?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because the Swindon warehouse scan for `JB-4491-0028-5GB` cleared the hardware return flag, but the recurring billing subscription token was left in 'Pending Final Bill' status.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So it is a complete failure in S-Net's own billing software! Why didn't the system stop the Direct Debit when the line closed and the router arrived?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When a cease order hangs in 'Pending Final Bill' status due to a stuck overnight batch script, the recurring Direct Debit mandate continues to trigger on the 15th.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is outrageous. You have taken three payments that you had zero right to take, leaving me short on my rent money this week.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: How much is the monthly charge amount that has been coming out of your bank account?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you even listening to me? I have already told you twice that it is £44 a month—£132 in total across August, September, and October!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Right, £44 a month. Hold on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have checked the ledger permissions on my terminal.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Again you just went dead silent on the line for almost a full minute! Have you processed my £132 refund back to my bank card now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: No, I haven't processed a refund because my screen doesn't let me edit billing buckets on an account where the broadband service status is marked inactive.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: What do you mean you haven't processed it? You just admitted your own system left the billing token stuck after the 4th of July!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Once an account is marked closed on our CRM, billing adjustments sit with the former-customer collections team—you'll have to write to them or ring their number.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Write to them?! You took £132 from my bank account by mistake and you're telling me I have to write a letter or chase another department myself?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is how the departmental split works here. Active accounts are handled by Frontline Customer Services and closed accounts sit with Former-Customer Collections.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can't you raise an internal ticket, transfer me warmly to a manager in that team, or clear the stuck billing flag yourself right now?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: They don't take internal warm transfers from our queue, and my user profile doesn't have the override button to close out a stuck final bill.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait, so if you don't close the stuck final bill today, is your system going to take ANOTHER £44 out of my account on the 15th of November?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Until the Former-Customer Collections team manually purges the recurring subscription token on their ledger, the Direct Debit request will remain scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Are you hearing yourself right now, Callum?! You're telling me S-Net is going to steal another £44 next month unless I do your job for you!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Raising your voice at me isn't going to make the money appear in your bank account any faster, is it?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Don't speak to me with that sarcastic attitude! You have been rude, unhelpful, and completely indifferent since I came on the line!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am telling you what the system allows me to do. I cannot click a button that is greyed out on my screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: A supervisor or team leader in your building certainly has authority to unstick a billing order and refund £132! Put me through to your manager.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Team leaders on this floor have the exact same CRM view for closed accounts as agents do, so speaking to a supervisor here won't change the process.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So what is this number or postal address you expect me to contact since you refuse to lift a finger to help me?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Former-Customer Billing & Collections number is `0800 098 4412`, and they are open Monday to Friday between 9:00 AM and 5:00 PM.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And have you at least put notes on my account with the Royal Mail tracking number `JB-4491-0028-5GB` and the cease reference `CEA-902184-SN`?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will need to quote those reference numbers to the advisor when you get through to the `0800 098 4412` queue.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You haven't even typed the notes into the account box after asking me all those questions for the first five minutes?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The notes box on an inactive service record only saves if a financial adjustment transaction is submitted at the same time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am cancelling my Direct Debit mandate directly with my bank today and raising an Indemnity Claim for all three £44 payments.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You can contact your bank if you choose, though you should still ring `0800 098 4412` so they don't flag the £132 clawback as an unpaid balance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: If S-Net dares to flag an unpaid balance on an account that was closed on the 4th of July, I will take it straight to Ofcom and the Ombudsman.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you want to log a formal complaint reference, you can ask the advisor on `0800 098 4412` to open one when they review the ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: You won't even log a complaint reference for me on this call?!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Complaint tickets on closed accounts have to be attached to the Former-Customer department's queue so their case handlers can see it.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you at least send me an email confirming that the Swindon warehouse scanned my router back in on the 10th of July?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Outbound email templates are disabled on terminated accounts, so I cannot trigger an email from this screen.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Every single thing I ask you to do, you just make up another excuse to do nothing.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Those are the system rules for inactive accounts on our CRM platform.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is hands down the worst customer service experience I have ever had with any utility company in the UK.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You have the `0800 098 4412` contact number for the team that handles former-customer billing adjustments.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I wrote the number down. Not that you have actually resolved a single thing I called up about.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else you want to ask about the active services side today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I have no active services with S-Net and after this ordeal I never will again.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Unbelievable. Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have a good day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, whatever.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net, goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Bye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Goodbye.
